risk_reasons: Changes the authorization path of the Admin API: every /api/admin/** mutation route reaches requireAdminWithAal2, and a defect here is an admin control-plane bypass.
Adds a second Admin transport (bearer) that carries the same trust as the session cookie; a weaker bearer arm would let a revoked or aal1 admin act.
Touches src/lib/db/auth.ts, the owner-classified auth gate (invariant #15 composition root) reached by ~40 owner and mixed-role routes via requireRoleOr401.
goal: requireAdminWithAal2 returns a Verified admin from EITHER Admin transport — the session cookie or a Supabase access token in Authorization: Bearer — refusing both transports through one byte-for-byte refusal contract, with requireAdminJson and resolveAdminActor inheriting it by composition and requireRole staying cookie-only.
non_goals: No route file changes: the nine role-only admin GET handlers stay on requireRole/requireRoleOr401 (#1184).
No src/proxy.ts change and no CSRF change — branch 4 still 401s a bearer-only request before the route, and withSameOriginUnlessBearer does not exist yet (#1185).
No CORS and no ADMIN_APP_ORIGINS (#1186); the Admin app still cannot call cross-origin after this ticket.
No change to scripts/ci/admin-aal2-audit.ts: the allowlist, the three credited gate shapes and the ROUTES contract are untouched (#1184 widens them).
No change to requireRole, requireRoleOr401 or any owner gate behaviour.
No MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED read in the seam or the gate (ADR 0025 D10).
No impersonation code touched beyond reading it.
No migration, no feature flag, no env var, no new dependency.
user_visible_behavior: An Admin API request carrying Authorization: Bearer <valid aal2 admin token> is authorized by requireAdminWithAal2 with transport 'bearer' — reachable today only from a non-browser caller, because src/proxy.ts still refuses it at branch 4.
A cookie-mode admin request behaves as before: same identity read, same strict aal2 test, same success.
A request whose Authorization header is present but not a well-formed 'Bearer <token>' is refused 401 {error:'Unauthorized'} and NEVER falls back to the session cookie.

A verified credential whose users row is missing, or whose role is not admin, is refused 403 {error:'Forbidden'} — a change from today's 401 on the missing-users-row cookie case, per the ticket's refusal table.

An unreadable AAL (Supabase error, no data, or a bearer whose aal claim is missing/non-string) is refused 403 {error:'mfa_check_failed'}; a readable AAL that is not 'aal2' is refused 403 {error:'mfa_required'}.
Every refusal carries NO_STORE_HEADERS and is a JSON response — never a redirect.
An owner route still rejects a bearer-only request 401: requireRole reads cookies only.
invariants: Invariant #8: users.auth_id maps to the Supabase Auth identity; the seam returns authUserId (the auth identity) and loadAppUser is the only mapper to a users row.
Invariant #15: only composition roots import @/lib/db/server. src/lib/db/auth.ts keeps that import (it is on ci:db-imports' allowlist); src/lib/auth/verified-identity.ts must NOT import it.
Invariant #13: no NEXT_PUBLIC_* companion and no new feature flag; MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED is never read below the proxy.
ci:admin-aal2 keeps crediting requireAdminWithAal2, requireAdminJson and resolveAdminActor with unchanged exported names and result shapes.
Verified admin means authentic + live + aal2 on BOTH transports: bearer mode pays a getUser round-trip and is never made cheaper than cookie mode.
One predicate owns 'is this bearer mode'; src/proxy.ts imports the same module in #1185 — no second copy of the header test.
The bearer predicate module is Edge-safe: no node: import, no DB, no Supabase client construction.
requireRole and requireRoleOr401 stay cookie-only: their auth surface does not widen.
edge_cases: Authorization header present but malformed (Basic, bare 'Bearer', empty value, 'Bearer  ' whitespace-only) → bearer transport is chosen and the request is refused 401 Unauthorized; the cookie is ignored. isBearerRequest is header PRESENCE, readBearerToken is well-formedness — the ticket's owed test binds presence, and ADR 0025 D6's 'well-formed bearer' phrasing for src/proxy.ts is served by readBearerToken, which #1185 may use instead. Both refuse, so the two consumers cannot disagree into a bypass.
Bearer scheme match is case-insensitive ('bearer', 'BEARER') per RFC 7235; the token itself is taken verbatim.
getClaims succeeds and claims.aal is missing or not a string → aal is null → 403 mfa_check_failed (not mfa_required).
Cookie mode: getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel returns error or no data → aal null → 403 mfa_check_failed (today's behaviour, preserved).

Cookie mode: getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel returns { currentLevel: null } with no error → aal null → 403 mfa_check_failed. Today this returns mfa_required. The state is unreachable after a successful getUser (a live session always carries aal1 or aal2), and the ticket's refusal table binds both transports to the same mapping.
Cookie mode with no session → 401 Unauthorized (today's shape, via the seam rather than requireRole).
Verified credential, users row present, role='owner' → 403 Forbidden.
Verified credential, no users row → 403 Forbidden (today's cookie path returns 401; the ticket's table binds 403).

getClaims/getUser are called per request on a freshly constructed bearer client; auth-js caches JWKS in a module-global keyed by storageKey (sb-<project-ref>-auth-token, derived from the URL), so a per-request client still shares the 10-minute JWKS cache and pays no extra fetch.
resolveAdminActor reads businessId from the request body AFTER the gate; the bearer arm does not consume the body, so req.json() in the resolver still works.

401 Unauthorized for: any other returned getClaims error (AuthInvalidJwtError forged/garbage token, AuthSessionMissingError, a 4xx AuthApiError); data === null with no error; claims whose exp is missing or past; and getUser(jwt) returning { user: null } (the revocation arm).

Cookie mode getUser() returning { user: null } — with or without an AuthSessionMissingError — is 401 Unauthorized, never a 500: a returned cookie auth error must not be thrown into the gates internal_error handler.
loadAppUser throwing (network, pool exhaustion) reaches the gates catch and is 500 { error: internal_error }, preserving todays behaviour.

Bearer verification failure classification, measured against @supabase/auth-js 2.106.2 by live probe: getClaims does NOT funnel every bad token through its AuthError catch. decodeJWT regex-checks the segments then JSON.parses them (lib/helpers.js:153-157), so ew.e30.AA (header decodes to the single character open-brace) throws SyntaxError, bnVsbA.e30.AA (header decodes to null) throws TypeError on header.alg, and aaaa.bbbb.cccc throws Error Invalid UTF-8 sequence. The seams try therefore wraps each SDK await and nothing else, and ANY throw from those two awaits is 401 Unauthorized — the malformed-token boundary. Treating an escaping throw as 500 would let an unauthenticated caller force 500s on the admin control plane with a two-character token.

The 500 arm is driven entirely by the RETURNED error type — isAuthRetryableFetchError, or isAuthApiError whose (status ?? 500) >= 500 (a GoTrue HTTP 500 becomes AuthApiError(status 500), lib/fetch.js:72). That loses no observability because _request -> handleError raises an AuthError which both getClaims and getUser catch and RETURN, so every infrastructure fault arrives through that channel. Anything thrown OUTSIDE the two awaits — client construction, our own logic, loadAppUser — still reaches the gates catch as 500 internal_error.

The bearer arm calls getClaims(jwt, { allowExpired: true }) and enforces exp itself (exp <= Math.floor(Date.now()/1000), zero leeway, mirroring validateExp). allowExpired skips validateExp ONLY; signature verification is unchanged. This removes an unclassifiable exception channel rather than message-matching JWT has expired, which the house rule at src/lib/auth/reset-password-error.ts forbids. Expiry stays closed twice: this check and the getUser round-trip.

rollback_plan: Single PR, no migration and no flag. Revert the merge commit on main and re-deploy: the gate returns to cookie-only and no caller outside this repo depends on the bearer arm yet (src/proxy.ts still 401s bearer-only requests until #1185, and CORS does not exist until #1186). On staging, reset staging to origin/main per deployment-guide.md § Re-sync staging.
observability: internalError('[admin-mfa-gate] unexpected failure:', err) keeps emitting the structured console.error for a seam or loadAppUser throw — the signal that distinguishes a Supabase/network fault from a legitimate 401/403.

A bearer refusal is distinguishable from a cookie refusal in Vercel logs by the presence of the Authorization header on the request; no new log line is added, and no token or claim value is ever logged.
